### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. <details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **213** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **153** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **153**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **98** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce001f97abbe460d9a6cc9a4bde6c6e38c9d37f8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `cd941396609e2930e2e2792b5359279f6b484866` — the merge of head `8454de72440b7bef7a411e4899b8d126f3f5f09c` into base `ce001f97abbe460d9a6cc9a4bde6c6e38c9d37f8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin cd941396609e2930e2e2792b5359279f6b484866 && git checkout cd941396609e2930e2e2792b5359279f6b484866
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ce001f97abbe460d9a6cc9a4bde6c6e38c9d37f8
```

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8454de72440b7bef7a411e4899b8d126f3f5f09c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-protocol-handshake.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-dependency-missing.test.ts + packages/cli/src/commands/package/install.ts (the sender, read on `main`), packages/metadata-core/src/protocol-handshake.ts (`assertProtocolCompat`, unchanged), packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts (`ManifestSchema`), packages/qa/dogfood/test/install-local-*.dogfood.test.ts (six files that build the lifted body), the plugin hunks of open PRs #28587 and #28554

Face: narrowing — `record-recognisers --paths` on the four changed paths decides no face (no published schema, no governed path); the changeset's `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line alone sets it. No further face is owed.

Ruling read: card #28535, triage 6554172575 ("measure with the CLI binary first, then fix whichever side owns the shape"; no second handshake, the 422 `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE` that `POST /packages` gives), claim 6554580917, the seat's order, dev report 6555096778. The dev measured with the real binary on base and head (transcripts quoted in the PR body) and chose the door: on `main` the bare compiled artifact is already flattened and refused, so the shape the door was built for is ADR-0130 D4's and only its detection guard was sender-dependent. That reading is right: fixing the CLI would leave every shipped CLI bypassing the handshake, and the ruling named the side that owns the contract.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The one hunk.** `normalizeBundle` was `m && !m.id && !m.name && isObject(m.manifest) && (m.manifest.id || m.manifest.name) ? { ...meta, ...sections } : m`; it is now `isPlainObject(m) ? flattenPackageBody(m) : m`, where `flattenPackageBody` (L545) is `isPlainObject(body.manifest) ? { ...meta, ...sections } : body`. Same spread, same order; only the guard changed. Correct as described.

2. **Exactly which bodies move.** A body whose `manifest` is a plain object AND which carries a top-level `id` or `name` — that is the shape `install.ts` L171-173 builds (`{ ...artifact, id: artifact.manifest.id ?? artifact.id, version: … }`) — was not flattened before and is now. Everything below that read a manifest-top-level key on that body now reads the real value: `engines` (step 1c, `assertProtocolCompat`), `dependencies` (step 1c', `checkDeclaredDependencies`), and `name` reaches the registered package. So the accept-set narrows by exactly: the lifted CLI shape whose `engines.protocol` excludes this runtime (422 `OS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE`) or whose `dependencies` are unmet (422 `DEPENDENCY_MISSING`). Nothing widens: no body that was refused before is admitted now (the old guard only ever withheld a flatten; it refused nothing). Declaration `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` correct.

3. **Conflict rule between a top-level key and the nested manifest's key.** `{ ...meta, ...sections }` — the top-level (section) key wins. For the CLI body the lifted `id`/`version` are copies of the nested ones, so identity is unchanged; the new `lit control` case pins `registered.id`, `registered.engines`, `registered.manifest` undefined and the ledger file's flat `engines`. For a hand-built body where they differ (no first-party sender builds one), the top-level value wins — and that is the order `flattenPackageBody` already applied at the unmanaged import (L3159) and the order its doc cites from `AssembledPackageBodySchema`. Before this change, `declaredPackageManifest` (install mode, namespace) read the NESTED value on such a body while the unmanaged import copied the TOP value; now both read the same flat body, so the two readers agree. One flatten, one rule: matches.

4. **Unchanged paths.** A flat manifest has no `manifest` key (`ManifestSchema` is a `strictObject`, L485, with no such key), so `flattenPackageBody` returns it as is — identity, exactly as before. The bare compiled artifact (no lifted id) was flattened by the old guard and is flattened by the new one — identical result; the `refuses the bare compiled artifact` case is a control green on base. A multi-package artifact (`packages[]`, no nested `manifest` at the top) is untouched on both branches, and the 1c' per-entry read of `entry.manifest` is unchanged. The catalog branch (`normalizeBundle(data?.manifest)`) applies the same rule: a published payload is the compiled bundle without a lifted id, flattened before and now; one that did carry a lifted id would now be read the same way as the inline one, which is the stated intent (ADR-0130 D4, one shape per door).

5. **Edge the old guard carried.** A body with a nested plain-object `manifest` that has neither `id` nor `name` was left nested before and is flattened now. No sender builds it; the result is then judged by the id gate (1b) as any flat body is. Acceptable and consistent with the unmanaged-import flatten.

6. **Controls hold.** `^18` lifted body: 200, `[protocol]` warnings `[]` (the false "declares no engines.protocol range" WARN is gone — a correctness gain, not a contract change: the warning was wrong). No-`engines` lifted body: 200 with exactly one `[protocol]` warning naming the id, as before. `^17` lifted body: `expectProtocolRefusal` (422, code, message, five `details` fields), `expectNothingWritten` (no register, no sync, no ledger file), no warning. Dependency: 422 `DEPENDENCY_MISSING` naming `com.example.sales`/`6.x`/`absent`, nothing written; installs once the dependency is present in range.

7. **Envelope identity.** `JSON.stringify(viaCli) === JSON.stringify(viaFlat)` pins the lifted body against the flat manifest. Parity with `POST /packages` transits: the existing `the two package-install doors give the same answer` group pins the flat manifest against `/packages`, and the lifted body reaches step 1c as that same flat object; the one `assertProtocolCompat` and the one `protocolIncompatibleAnswer` helper are untouched. No second handshake, as the ruling requires.

8. **Nothing ledgered on refusal.** Both refusals sit at 1c/1c', ahead of the hot-register (step 3) and the ledger write (L2018); `expectNothingWritten` covers register, sync and the storage dir in the new cases.

9. **First-party callers and what they now get.** CLI `os package install ./dist/objectstack.json` (install.ts L214): a mismatched artifact now exits 1 with the 422 the CLI already renders (measured transcript in the PR); compatible ones install with no false WARN. CLI untouched, correct: the lift is harmless under this door and the door owns the shape. objectui Console (`marketplaceApi.ts` L860-866) posts `{ packageId, versionId?, installMode? }` — the catalog branch, no inline manifest — unchanged. Six dogfood tests build the lifted body (`install-local-listing-not-loaded`, `-listing-sample-data`, `-no-active-organization`, `-purge-sample-data`, `-sample-data-not-loaded`, `-connector-spec-file`); all install compatible artifacts, and their ledger entries are now stored flat. `listing-not-loaded` edits `crm.manifest.engines` at the top of the stored entry, which is where the flat entry keeps it, so it still pins what it pinned. The dev's local dogfood battery on this head: 364 files / 2934 tests passed; the CI dogfood shards are skipped on `pull_request` events by design (`ci.yml` L2391), so that local run is the evidence for the dogfood face.

10. **#28604 (boot rehydrate reads stored lifted entries unflattened).** Out of scope here and not made worse: the rehydrate (L997) and the purge/reseed judge (L3569) read `entry.manifest` as stored, untouched by this diff. Entries this door writes from now on are flat (pinned by the ledger assertion in the new lit control), so the rehydrate reads them correctly; only entries written by a pre-fix install keep the lifted shape, which is exactly #28604's reach.

11. **Overlap.** This PR's only hunk on the plugin is `@@ -1444,13 +1444,19 @@`. PR #28587's plugin hunks are at L650, L1018, L1947; PR #28554's at L233, L511, L1924, L2102, L3020 (insertions beside, not inside, the flatten helpers at L520-549). No textual overlap with either; `flattenPackageBody` itself is not edited by any of the three. PR #28571's `handleUninstall` hunks are untouched.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cloud-connection: patch`. AGENTS.md step 3: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition. The changeset carries both declaration lines (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: none`), the `**BREAKING**` banner, and exactly one marker `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; its body prescribes no consumer rewrite (nothing an author writes is added, removed or re-shaped — the refusals are the existing shared answers), so the category's one mechanical check holds. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: no key, value or meaning an author writes changed. Title carries `!` and matches the changeset's first line. The `Check Changeset` job (which runs `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` against the merge base) is green on this head. Level and declarations consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none. Nothing to answer.
- Out-of-scope finding (rehydrate reads the stored lifted shape): filed as #28604 by the seat; confirmed out of scope and not worsened (① item 10). Not this PR's to fix.
- Noted-not-filed (rebase order against #28587): no hunk overlap verified (① item 11); the order is the seat's call and needs no change here.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no second login to name.
- Check-runs on this head at read time: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Test Core` shards 3/8 and 7/8 complete and green; the remaining `Test Core` shards and the `Lint` family still in progress or queued, nothing red. Landing-check ② (all green) is the seat's read at landing, not this record's.
- Draft, no auto-merge armed. Nothing to disarm.

### ④ Design judgment

Narrowing face, no `hits`: the narrowing judged against the published contract on `main`. ADR-0087 D1 says the handshake runs before a package's metadata is loaded, and `skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md` and `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx` already state that every install door refuses an out-of-range app and runs the pre-install dependency check; no page described the CLI artifact path as an exception. So this change takes no declared capability away from a consumer — it makes the spec's own refusal real at the one sender that escaped it. The fix is at the right layer: the door reads the shape it receives, not the sender's identity; the old guard was a sender-shaped exception, and removing it leaves one flatten (`flattenPackageBody`) serving the inline branch, the catalog branch and the unmanaged import, with `declaredPackageManifest` now an identity read on both branches (left in place, still stating where each shape keeps its keys — acceptable). Against the four axes: a real deployment path (the air-gapped install an administrator uses without a catalog); contract-first (one handshake, one dependency check, one flatten, no `??` fallback); it makes the wrong thing loud (an AI-built artifact for another protocol is refused at the boundary instead of loading half-working under a false warning); and it adds no new gate or surface. The tests build the body exactly as `install.ts` builds it, which is the scenario the card accepts against. Holds.
